(PER: THE HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA)
1. Heard Sri.Akash, who appears before this Court physically and represents Sri. Y. Lakshmikant Reddy, learned counsel on record for the appellant.

Also heard Sri. G. N. Raichur, who appears through Video Conference and represents respondent No.3.
2.

Challenge in this appeal is to the award that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VII,
Hospet in MVC No.601/2011 dated 10.02.2016.

This is a claimant's appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:15174 HC-KAR 3.

On the ground that he sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred in the year 2010, the appellant, who was aged around 8 years as on the date of accident, filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- in total.
The Tribunal through the impugned award granted a sum of Rs.3,26,000/- as compensation.

With a version that he is entitled to a higher sum,
the present appeal is filed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the disability as assessed by PW2 is 73.3% in respect of right ear and the disability as assessed by PW3 is 10% in respect of right lower limb.
But the Tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 30% which is improper.

Learned counsel also states that the Tribunal failed to award any compensation for the expenses which the parents of the appellant incurred for food, extra nourishment, attendant and NC: 2025:KHC-D:15174 HC-KAR conveyance charges.
Learned counsel thereby seeks enhancement in compensation.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 on the other hand states that the disability as assessed by the Tribunal is proper and thereby the compensation granted by the Tribunal is on proper lines and thus the appeal is not maintainable.
6. Having considered the totality of evidence produced, the Tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 30% which needs no interference.

Also placing reliance upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Master Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd.,1 the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- as compensation for the functional disability in respect of whole body.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, as rightly projected, Tribunal failed to award any compensation to compensate the appellant for (2014) 14 SCC 396 NC: 2025:KHC-D:15174 HC-KAR food, extra nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges which the parents of the appellant would have incurred during the period of treatment of the appellant and thereafter till his recovery.

7. Taking into consideration the fact that the accident occurred in the year 2010, basing on the rupee value of the said period and the availability of goods and services, the Court is of the view that the amount which the appellant's parents could have incurred for food, extra nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges might be Rs.25,000/- in total.
8. Therefore, this Court is of the view that the compensation that is granted by the Tribunal is required to be enhanced by Rs.25,000/-.

9. Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following order:
NC: 2025:KHC-D:15174 HC-KAR ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VII,
Hospet through orders in MVC No.601/2011 dated 10.02.2016 is enhanced by Rs.25,000/-.
iii. The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv. Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
v. On such deposit, appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount subject to producing sufficient proof that he has attained the age of majority.
